evidence: Context reliance drops during instruction finetuning on TULU, Alpaca, UltraChat; Llama, Mistral, Pythia; controlled studies; theoretical analysis; mitigation with limited gains.
rationale: Hedged 'may not' title backed by inversion across several named datasets and model families; abstract claims stay modest, mitigation gains described as limited.

evidence: Closed-form large-qubit-limit generalization formulas; bandwidth moves model from provably no generalization to good generalization for well-aligned targets; unnamed datasets confirm predictions.
rationale: H6: 'Enables' drops the well-aligned-target condition. Abstract claims theory predicts behaviour on datasets far outside assumptions, none named (H4).

evidence: PerContrast up to 87.8% F1 on own benchmark; PerCE on multiple unnamed LLMs, average >10%, up to 40.57% on LongLaMP; transfer claims unspecified.
rationale: Title supported by gains from upweighting personal tokens. 'Strong cross-task and cross-scenario transferability' without naming tested tasks or scenarios is mild scope (H4).

evidence: Training-free MCMC-style sampler over different base models; MATH500, HumanEval, GPQA; nearly matches or beats RL; avoids diversity collapse.
rationale: Title paraphrase (base models hold more reasoning than assumed) supported across several base models and three named benchmarks; broad-applicability claim is hedged ('suggesting').

evidence: Unspecified experiments: clustering aligns with known annotator behaviour; L2D-Clusters comparable to expert-specific L2D, esp. onboarding with limited data.
rationale: Descriptive title. Abstract claims only comparable performance, a modest direction claim supported by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Pre-training on COCO, Visual Genome, CC, SBU; conditioned vs unconditioned masking; ablation; SOTA on six V+L tasks/nine datasets incl. VQA, VCR, NLVR2.
rationale: 'Universal' attribute backed by SOTA across six named V+L tasks; SOTA on named benchmarks is not overreach (rule 2).

evidence: Mechanistic study of trained Gemma 7B frequency usage; mathematical proofs of RoPE behaviours; unspecified experiments; RoPE modification improves performance.
rationale: Question title; findings scoped to Gemma 7B and argued with hedges ('unlikely', 'suspect', 'believe'); modification claims only direction of improvement.

evidence: FIM equals variance of input Jacobian; closed-form spectral bounds for ReLU, convolution; theoretical comparison VGG/ResNet/DenseNet/Transformer; power iteration/Hutchinson estimators; unspecified experiments.
rationale: 'Practical Algorithms' plausibly matched: estimators are used in experiments demonstrating utility. Abstract claims (validation, utility) stay at direction level of unspecified experiments.

evidence: Omniglot one-shot 98.1→98.5%, few-shot 98.9→99.3%; TIMIT speech task tested but no result reported.
rationale: Imperative 'Make SVM great' describes the method; Omniglot gains support it. 'Eliminates the problem of choosing a correct kernel' is absolute wording without evidence (H3).

evidence: Unspecified BWN training study (STE, BN): scaling factors marginal, sign changes crucial, signs fixed early, kernels concentrated; QBN proposed without results.
rationale: Title's importance-of-signs claim matches the reported direction. Compression hypothesis is hedged ('may', 'hope'); no own result asserted beyond the study.

evidence: Convergence proofs (non-convex, PL, strongly convex); accelerated version provably faster than basic; QSGD implementation; unspecified experiments show superiority over several algorithms.
rationale: Acceleration from past-dependent (Markovian, momentum) schemes is backed by theorems and experiments; superiority is a direction claim over existing methods.

evidence: Unspecified image-based continuous control tasks; compared with VAE representations, model-free and model-based RL; final performance and sample efficiency.
rationale: Descriptive title. 'Substantially' and 'much more efficiently' are magnitude claims backed only by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Scrambled-word transfer in four classification and two sequence labeling tasks; LSTMs with GloVe, BERT, baselines; only BERT transfers, for classification only.
rationale: Activity gerund title. Abstract findings are explicitly scoped to tested models and task types, framed as a partial answer.

evidence: BERT-fused NMT; supervised sentence/document-level, semi-supervised, unsupervised translation; SOTA on seven unnamed benchmark datasets.
rationale: Descriptive title. State-of-the-art claim on seven unnamed datasets is a SOTA claim backed only by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Structure-aware vocabulary via Foldseek; pretraining on ~40M proteins; surpasses unnamed established baselines on 10 unnamed downstream tasks.
rationale: Descriptive title. 'General-purpose', 'exceptional capacity and broad applicability' exceed unnamed tasks and baselines; magnitude and breadth unsupported by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Unspecified experiments showing two hyperparameter-dependent training pathways; theoretical analysis in a simplified setting; cross-dataset non-robust features (hedged).
rationale: H6: title states robust-before-non-robust unconditionally, but abstract says it holds only for one hyperparameter-dependent pathway. Abstract findings are hedged or conditional.

evidence: Procedural puzzle generator with DAG dependencies and ground-truth solutions; experiments reveal limits of unnamed multimodal LLM/VLM agents.
rationale: Descriptive title. Benchmark properties follow from construction; testbed value is hedged ('we hope'); no priority claim.

evidence: none reported
rationale: Descriptive title. 'Can reduce the variance of the gradient estimation' and 'combines the merits' are design rationale with no experiment or theorem (H1).

evidence: Unspecified extensive experiments on learning rate rewinding, weight rewinding, fine-tuning, 1-cycle schedule; randomly pruned beats methodically pruned with right schedule.
rationale: Evaluative 'That Matters' title fits findings. Large-learning-rate explanation is supported by reported (unspecified) experiments; no breadth or magnitude claims.

evidence: Unnamed challenging offline RL benchmarks; compared to state-of-the-art model-free and model-based approaches.
rationale: Gerund title, no claim. Beats SOTA on unnamed benchmarks; variance reduction and 'better rewards' from Lagrange multipliers are design rationale without measurement (H1).

evidence: Theoretical framework for disentanglement guarantees under weak supervision with distribution matching; empirical verification for restricted labeling, match-pairing, rank-pairing.
rationale: 'With Guarantees' matches a framework that derives guarantees and limitations, empirically verified on named weak-supervision methods.

evidence: High-norm artifact tokens in supervised and self-supervised ViTs; register tokens remove artifacts; SOTA on unnamed dense prediction tasks; smoother maps.
rationale: H7: 'Need' title backed by improvements; 'fixes that problem entirely' is absolute wording; SOTA on unnamed dense tasks rests on unspecified experiments.

evidence: SOTA on unnamed public benchmarks and own ad banner dataset; user study preference over baselines by significant margins.
rationale: 'Is a good layout designer' supported by results and user study. SOTA and 'significant margins' rest on unnamed benchmarks and an unquantified study.

evidence: Theoretical bounds on classifier susceptibility; adversarial examples inescapable for certain problem classes; experiments on dimensionality and image complexity effects.
rationale: Question title answered for certain problem classes only, so matched not understated; abstract scopes its inevitability claim.

evidence: Two audio retrieval tasks: query-by-humming music search and speech search by audio query; outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
rationale: Descriptive title. 'For any kind of audio' exceeds two tested tasks; efficiency and faster matching are design claims never measured (H1).

evidence: Theorem: probabilistic transformer outputs in compact K with expected output approximating continuous f; deep Berge maximum theorem; classical transformers only for convex constraints.
rationale: Title drops 'probabilistic' and expectation conditions; classical transformers covered only for convex constraints. Unhedged 'the first universal approximation theorem' is a priority claim (H5).

evidence: ImageNet: less overconfidence, order-of-magnitude confidence reduction on context-only images; class activation maps; +0.021 AP on MS COCO transfer.
rationale: Idiom paraphrased as negated universal (fixed smoothing not right for all images), supported by adaptive-smoothing counterexample; abstract claims quantified on named datasets.

evidence: SimPLe on range of Atari games at 100k interactions; outperforms state-of-the-art model-free algorithms in most games, some by >10x.
rationale: Descriptive title. SOTA comparison on named Atari benchmark with quantified gains and 'in most games' qualifier stays within evidence.

evidence: Unnamed range of MIP problems; beats state-of-the-art learning-based models and SCIP; often outperforms Gurobi.
rationale: 'Towards' title is matched. Claim that the value function reduces training complexity and enhances sample quality is design rationale without reported measurement (H1).

evidence: 2,671 expert-validated QA pairs; frontier model accuracies from 34% to 72%; models struggle on higher-order architecture reasoning.
rationale: Descriptive title. Unhedged 'the first benchmark' for computer architecture is a priority claim without evidence (H5).

evidence: With ε=8, 74.9% CIFAR10 and 95.1% SVHN test accuracy, improving over existing results.
rationale: Prescriptive title matched by accuracy at modest privacy. 'Greatly helps to break the dimensional barrier' and low computational cost are design rationale, unmeasured (H1).

evidence: Backtracking Llama-3-8B unsafe rate 6.1%→1.5% without helpfulness regression; protection against four adversarial attacks.
rationale: Title claim about the technique is supported. 'Models trained to backtrack are consistently safer' generalises from one reported model (H2).

evidence: Hundreds of GPT-style transformers, 500K–1.5B parameters; capacity ≈3.6 bits/parameter; grokking onset at capacity; scaling laws for membership inference.
rationale: Question title answered with quantified estimate across many trained models; matched rather than understated given restricted model range. Abstract claims stay within measurements.

evidence: Unspecified experiments: beats existing deep learning models on vision metrics; improves 3D structure matching, loop reconstruction, domain boundaries; human cell reproducibility.
rationale: Descriptive title. Claims are direction-level improvements over existing models; real-world applicability phrased as purpose, not as a result.

evidence: ELMo-style code embeddings fine-tuned for bug detection; low-dimensional embedding from small corpus improves an unnamed state-of-the-art bug detector.
rationale: Descriptive title. Improving a state-of-the-art system is a direction claim; 'not previously applied' is framed as field background.

evidence: Unspecified demonstrations: plausible diverse variations from single scene; merits over state-of-the-art neural scene generators; 3D editing, composition, animation applications.
rationale: Activity gerund title. 'Generative model for general natural scenes' claims generality beyond unspecified evaluated scenes.

evidence: Crafting-based grid world dataset of human instructions and trajectories; solves complex tasks; zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks; few-shot learning.
rationale: Prescriptive 'Ask Your Humans' for generalization in RL broadly, but evidence covers one grid-world environment. Abstract claims stay within that setting.

evidence: RAVEn on LRS3: beats all self-supervised VSR methods; 30h labels beat 90,000h semi-supervised; SOTA low-resource ASR and VSR.
rationale: Activity gerund title. SOTA claims tied to named LRS3; viability conclusion hedged ('point to').

evidence: Conv modules match attention at similar cost (unspecified); consistent gains on deblurring, denoising, deraining with less computation.
rationale: 'Architecture Matters' supported by attention-replacement analysis and restoration gains; abstract claims are direction-level across tested tasks.

evidence: Synthetic and real-world datasets with artificial vertical partitioning (unnamed); matches accuracy of centralized methods.
rationale: Descriptive title. Unhedged 'the first framework' (H5); 'guaranteeing privacy' is absolute with no proof or privacy evaluation reported (H3).

evidence: Unspecified initial study: transfer quality of continually pretrained representations shows no noticeable degradation; GLAD proposed with no reported results.
rationale: Title asserts incremental generalization; evidence shows only no degradation. GLAD efficiency and barrier-breaking claims lack results (H1); 'novel problem' is unhedged priority (H5).

evidence: Explicit (2N+4)L-layer transformer simulating L GD steps of N-layer ReLU nets; approximation/convergence guarantees; softmax extension; synthetic 3/4/6-layer tests.
rationale: Title generalises to pretrained transformers, but evidence is a constructed transformer of specific depth; condition dropped. Abstract scopes results to construction and synthetic data.

evidence: Unspecified extensive experiments and ablations on LLM-guided Bayesian optimization for molecular discovery.
rationale: Activity gerund title. 'Substantially improves scalability, robustness, and sample efficiency' is a magnitude claim backed only by unspecified experiments.

evidence: Benchmark design: explicit perceptual and implicit manipulative evaluation, HF-Embodied dataset, preference evaluator, three embodied scenarios; no results reported.
rationale: 'Towards' title fits. Unhedged 'first step in evaluating World Simulators' (H5); evaluator alignment and 'key insights' asserted without reported results.

evidence: 17 attention/gated-conv LMs on the Pile; 2.1 ppl gap, 82% from associative recall; 70M attention beats 1.4B; hybrids close 97.4%.
rationale: Measuring/improving title supported by quantified analyses; 'large margin' is backed by reported numbers.

evidence: Embodied, web navigation, tool-use domains; up to 45.67% success gain on ALFWorld; generalization across unnamed agent architectures and LLM backbones.
rationale: Descriptive title. Generalization 'across different agent architectures and LLM backbones' without naming what was tested is mild scope (H4).

evidence: Unspecified qualitative and quantitative experiments: mini-batch SGD rarely crosses barriers; large-batch gradients align with top Hessian eigenvectors.
rationale: Question title; abstract reports experimental findings with a hedged mechanism; causal explanation is backed by reported (unspecified) evidence.

evidence: Theoretical results: context-based fine-tuning cannot change relative attention patterns, only biases attention outputs in a fixed direction; less expressive than full fine-tuning.
rationale: 'When do ... work?' title answered by expressiveness results; implications hedged ('potentially', 'suggests', 'may not').

evidence: Dual-head GPT-2-small; GPT-4o-generated dataset of primitives (add, subtract, max, min, sort); decoder raises execution accuracy 0.58→0.82; near-zero counting errors.
rationale: Title claims boosting 'LLMs' on 'algorithmic tasks'; evidence is one GPT-2-small on simple primitives. Abstract's 'even small models' generalises from one model (H2).

evidence: Linear LR schedule shortens IMP retraining; adaptive initial value; budgeted dense training outperforms sparsify-during-training SOTA (unspecified experiments).
rationale: Paraphrase 'embrace retraining' matches findings. 'Massively shortened' and beating SOTA rest on unspecified experiments without numbers.
